narrative_summary: Abdominal pain is a significant clinical feature in various conditions. In TRAPS, it is the most prominent finding, particularly in childhood [S5|PMC8293050|1409]. Autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) can also present with abdominal pain, as seen in cases involving a 76-year-old male and a 64-year-old male [S4|PMC9355740|198][S6|PMC9355740|230]. Histopathological features of vitamin E deficiency include steatitis and muscle degeneration, with widespread adipocyte necrosis [S2|PMC7149534|9]. In TRAPS, histopathology reveals a lymphocytic infiltrate with venule cuffing [S5|PMC8293050|1409]. Management of AIHA varies, with treatments including prednisolone and supportive RBC transfusions [S4|PMC9355740|198][S5|PMC9355740|229]. Risk factors such as inflammatory bowel disease and eosinophilic gastroenteritis are noted in specific populations [S3|PMC7149534|34].
